chapter: New York, Philadelphia and Harlem nightlife
title: Segregation on 52nd Street and elsewhere
summary: He describes places where blacks were not welcome, from Leon and Eddie's to the Theresa, and a Jack Dempsey's incident.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: 52nd Street was that way, wasn't it...up until...
Behind the post? Well, not really, and in one sense, yes. But I can't pinpoint it. Like Leon and

Eddie's, you know what I mean. Like...what's that other...21 Club, or whatever it was. You just didn't go in there. You didn't even go that way on 52nd Street. The buck stopped in the middle of the block. But, like Jimmy Ryan's...Jimmy Ryan's wasn't lily white, 'cause they had black musicians there, playing /and occasionally, you know what I mean, and people went in. But you had some spots where they...and that's amazing, too...that as late as the thirties you were having that kind of situation.

And even the Theresa. You couldn't get a room in the Theresa, you know what I mean, during some period back there. And you'd go in places and they'd give you a...you know what I mean...it's quite possible you could get a Mickey Finn, you know. I did something in Jack Dempsey's...they were kind of funny in there. So I was up a lot of stuff. I was with Tallulah Bankhead. I was up to a lot of stuff. And then I noticed, I gave them...like, the man's sleeve in the soup and a few other things. So I asked for the check and I gave a thousand dollar bill and I ran his ass all over Broadway trying to get that thing changed (laughter).
